He was occupied as a journalist, principally for Jewish newspapers and the Jewish Telegraphic Agency, until 1937, and he appears to have had extensive left wing connections. During 1937 he discontinued journalism and concentrated on business activities with Scophany Ltd., television engineers, (Manager: Solomon SAGALL, his brother) and with E.K. Cole Ltd., radio engineers; in October, 1938, he received £835 as commission for the sale of television equipment to the Soviet Government. In September, 1939, he obtained employment as manager to Dawney Day & Co. Ltd., merchant bankers, 15, Moorgate, E.C. Enquiry was made by Special Branch, at the request of M.I.5, into the allegation that SAGALL was purchasing arms factories in neutral European countries and report of 24th July, 1940, (320/EPA/9508) confirms this suggestion.

This man is frequently at 80-86 Regent Street, W., and is probably in close touch with URIEWICZ. It is quite possible that SAGALL may be used by URIEWICZ as a contact with the Soviet Embassy, as the sale of television apparatus to the Soviet Government by the former indicates some connection with the Embassy.

URIEWICZ is also in telephonic communication with Willesden 6976, the telephone number allotted to G.F. BIGGS, 78, Hillside, Stonebridge, N.W.10. Residing at this address is Frederick David BIGGS, subject of Special Branch report of 24th February, 1938 (301/MP/5457). This man was found to have Communist sympathies and was a subscriber to "The Week". He was, at the time of enquiry, employed as a labourer by the Hogarth Press, Hythe Road, Willesden, N.W.10.

Another acquaintance is Stanislaw RETZLAW, Pole, born 2nd June, 1898, at Inowaratslow, living at 11, Peters Court, Porchester Road, W.2, mentioned in Special Branch report of 9th January, 1941, (405/40/1434) who is said to have been acting as an agent for the British Government. URIEWICZ has said that this is not the man's correct name but he affirms that RETZLAW is a British agent.

URIEWICZ also professes to be working for the Polish Government on financial matters. He is making enquiries at many banking establishments with a view to purchasing French francs, and I am told the money is to be used for propaganda abroad. Enquiries of the Polish authorities show that URIEWICZ was authorised by them to conduct a purchase of 15,000 pengos on behalf of the Polish Minister of Finance, M. LURA. Briefly, Uriewicz was in contact with a Hungarian Jew (identity not disclosed) who had the necessary sum available in Hungary. An equivalent amount in sterling was paid to his account in this country and the pengos were released for use by Polish agents abroad. This transaction was completed two months ago, and URIEWICZ is not authorised to make any further negotiations in the name of the Polish Government.
